name: SE-Agent: Self-Evolution Trajectory Optimization in Multi-Step Reasoning with LLM-Based Agents
authors: Jiaye Lin, Yifu Guo, et al. (14 authors); lead affiliations Tsinghua University (THU) and StepFun, with PKU/UCAS/UofT/UCR/USYD/UMN collaborators
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (poster); arXiv preprint arXiv:2508.02085 (first submitted Aug 2025)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique + search-guided + population/evolutionary. The agent verbally reflects on each pilot trajectory (Reflect/Revise), then runs an evolutionary search over a pool of trajectories using three operators (revision, recombination, refinement). Conceptually a genetic-algorithm / expert-iteration style search rather than plain single-trajectory MCTS.
feedback_source: Mixed: (1) self-generated LLM critique (Reflect, ExpertEval) and (2) external-tool / rule-based structural validation (AutoEval: non-empty patch files, sufficient code-editing steps, reasonable trajectory length). Final reported success on SWE-bench Verified is measured by developer-written unit tests, but the in-loop trajectory selection reward is a weighted combination of AutoEval (rule-based) + LLM ExpertEval, not the held-out test oracle.
iteration_structure: population/evolutionary: starts from a pool of diverse initial 'pilot' trajectories (Gamma_0) and iteratively evolves generations Gamma_k via revision, recombination (crossover/transfer/restructuring) and refinement (multi-dimensional reward + elite selection), until convergence (max-reward improvement < epsilon) or a max iteration budget. Default 10 candidate trajectories, 5 distinct planning strategies for seeding.
reflection_object: action trajectory (the full multi-step reasoning/interaction trajectory). SE-Agent reflects on and manipulates entire pilot trajectories at the trajectory level (revising, recombining segments via crossover, and refining) rather than editing isolated output tokens or model weights. The underlying base LLM is frozen; only the trajectories/search are optimized.
requires_training: none — base LLMs are frozen and used as-is (plug-and-play wrapper around SWE-Agent / CodeAct). No SFT/RL/DPO weight updates; improvement comes entirely from inference-time evolutionary trajectory optimization.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge + verifiable-structural reward (no separately trained reward model). The multi-dimensional Reward(tau,t) = w1*TaskCompletion + w2*ReasoningQuality + w3*Efficiency, where TaskCompletion = AutoEval (rule-based structural checks) + lambda*ExpertEval (the LLM itself acting as judge). ReasoningQuality is LLM-judged.
distillation_target: none — reflections are not distilled into a persisted reusable artifact (no skill library, no weight update, no cross-task memory). Cross-trajectory insight lives only inside the current task's evolving trajectory pool and is discarded after the task; the final output is the single highest-reward trajectory tau*.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered / scaffold-engineered. The reflective and evolutionary behavior is explicitly prompt- and operator-engineered (revision, recombination, refinement operators with hand-designed prompts and a hand-designed reward), not RL-emergent like an R1-style 'aha' moment.
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad — the evolving trajectory pool (population of candidate trajectories for the current task) acts as working memory. No long-term episodic memory or persistent skill library.
memory_persistence: within-episode (per-task). The trajectory pool and cross-trajectory inspiration are confined to solving a single task; nothing is carried across tasks or sessions.
memory_curation_mechanism: population-or-Pareto-selected: each generation applies Select(Gamma_k ∪ Gamma_k' ∪ Gamma_k^new, o) to retain o elite trajectories by reward score while preserving diversity via trajectory-dissimilarity metrics, preventing the pool from ballooning and avoiding homogeneous collapse.
error_localization_granularity: holistic/trajectory-level (action-trajectory level). SE-Agent reflects on and operates over whole trajectories (and trajectory segments via crossover), identifying logical inconsistencies and under-developed reasoning steps across the trajectory rather than at token level. The case study frames the win as escaping step-local 'tunnel vision' to find a root-cause fix in a different file.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task: experience is reused across multiple trajectories of the SAME task (cross-trajectory inspiration within one task's evolution), not transferred across different tasks. No inter-task experience transfer like Reflexion/ExpeL.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: post-hoc-revision combined with avoidance via population search: suboptimal pilot trajectories are revised/recombined into improved ones and low-reward paths are pruned by selection, rather than correcting a single trajectory mid-flight.
task_domains: code (real-world software engineering / GitHub issue resolution). Framework is presented as general for multi-step reasoning (math, planning, creative tasks mentioned), but evaluated only on code/SWE.
benchmarks: SWE-bench Verified (500 curated real-world GitHub issues).
headline_result: On SWE-bench Verified, integrating SE-Agent yields up to 55% relative improvement and achieves SOTA among open-source agents. With Claude-3.7-Sonnet it reaches 61.2% Pass@1 (63.6% Pass@5) vs SWE-Agent 40.6% / SWE-Search 47.4%. A footnote reports 80.0% with Claude-4-Sonnet using the latest SWE-Agent (vs 66.6% baseline on the 2025-05-22 SWE-bench Verified leaderboard).
baselines: SWE-Agent (CodeAct-based) and SWE-Search (MCTS-based) — both strong open-source SWE frameworks. Evaluated across 5 LLMs: DeepSeek-V3-0324, Qwen-2.5-72b-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70b-Instruct (open-source), GPT-4o, Claude-3.7-Sonnet (closed-source).
gains_vs_baseline: Pass@1 vs SWE-Agent: +112% relative (Llama-3.1-70b: 15.4%->32.6%), +80% (GPT-4o: 22.4%->40.4%), +51% (Claude-3.7: 40.6%->61.2%); DeepSeek-V3 31.6%->54.8%, Qwen-2.5-72b 18.8%->38.8%. Vs the stronger MCTS-based SWE-Search: roughly +30% relative on average (e.g., Claude-3.7 47.4%->61.2%, DeepSeek-V3 39.4%->54.8%). SE-Agent also uniquely resolves 12 issues that no baseline solves.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-time multiplier: generates a pool of ~10 candidate trajectories per task (default), seeded by 5 planning strategies, plus revision/recombination/refinement passes — i.e., a multi-trajectory (population) search rather than a single pass. Authors report near-optimal performance at just 10 candidate trajectories and claim that, under matched maximum-API-cost budgets, SE-Agent still beats baselines on Pass@1; positioned as more efficient than open-ended Test-Time-Scaling. No exact token-count multiplier is given. No training cost (base models frozen).
known_limitations: No explicit Limitations section in the paper body. Practical limits inferable from the design/scope: (1) evaluated only on SWE-bench Verified (code), so generality to math/embodied/other domains is asserted but unverified (left to future work, e.g., DeepSearch, embodied intelligence); (2) inference cost scales with the trajectory-pool size and multiple operator passes; (3) the in-loop reward relies on LLM self-judgment (ExpertEval) plus hand-tuned weights (w1,w2,w3,lambda) and rule-based structural checks, which may be gamed or miscalibrated; (4) improvements are within-task only — no persistent learning/transfer across tasks.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier (partial). The in-loop signal blends self-verification (LLM ExpertEval/ReasoningQuality) with rule-based structural validation (AutoEval: non-empty patch, sufficient edit steps, trajectory length) — NOT the held-out unit-test oracle, which is used only for final scoring. So selection does not directly leak the ground-truth test labels; structural validators provide the external grounding.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive on the evaluated benchmark: consistent Pass@1/Pass@5 gains across all 5 LLMs over both CodeAct and MCTS baselines, with ablations showing each operator (revision, recombination, refinement) contributes and removing any one lowers Pass@1. Efficacy demonstrated only on SWE-bench Verified (code).
calibration_effect: not-measured — the paper does not analyze confidence calibration or a 'reasoning tax'; it reports task resolution rates only.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a — SE-Agent is a self-improvement / search method, not a failure-attribution method. It implicitly localizes weaknesses during the per-trajectory Reflect step (identifying logical inconsistencies / underdeveloped steps) but does not produce a failure taxonomy or attribute responsibility across agents.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets homogeneous/redundant search and local-optima 'tunnel vision' (near-identical rollouts that only tweak surface expressions), i.e., a diversity-collapse / underthinking-style failure where probabilistic LLMs gravitate to high-probability solution patterns. Loosely maps to MAST-style 'superficial self-reflection' and lack-of-exploration error loops; cross-trajectory recombination is the proposed remedy.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark released. Code and demonstration materials released at https://github.com/JARVIS-Xs/SE-Agent (uses existing SWE-bench Verified).
builds_on: SWE-Agent / agent-computer interface (Yang et al.) and CodeAct as the underlying code-agent scaffold; ReAct (Yao et al.) as the multi-turn reasoning paradigm; MCTS-based search (SWE-Search) as the primary search baseline it critiques and extends; Reflexion and CRITIC as self-improvement predecessors; conceptual roots in genetic/evolutionary algorithms and self-play / expert iteration.
extended_by_or_inspired: Part of the 2025 wave of self-evolving SWE agents; related/follow-up work includes Live-SWE-agent (arXiv:2511.13646, 'Can Software Engineering Agents Self-Evolve on the Fly?', Claude-4.5-Sonnet 75.4% on SWE-bench Verified) which positions itself against self-evolving open-source agents. (Full forward-citation list [uncertain].)
citation_count: ~31 (Semantic Scholar, mid-2026; ~43 per Google Scholar via arXiv listing)
reasoning_model_native: No — SE-Agent is model-agnostic and was evaluated on standard instruction-tuned chat/code LLMs (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen-2.5-72b, Llama-3.1-70b, GPT-4o, Claude-3.7/4-Sonnet), not o1/R1-style built-in-reflection reasoning models. It adds reflection externally via scaffolding, but is claimed to remain effective regardless of base-model improvements as long as tasks need multi-step reasoning.
on_policy_distillation_link: Weak/none. SE-Agent does not perform on-policy distillation or weight-level skill optimization; it is an inference-time evolutionary trajectory search with frozen models. Conceptually adjacent to expert-iteration / self-play (each trajectory-optimization step acts as an 'improvement operator'), but no policy is distilled into weights or a reusable skill artifact.
sample_efficiency: Reaches near-optimal performance with ~10 candidate trajectories per task (5 planning seeds + revision/recombination/refinement); authors emphasize 'remarkably fewer evolutionary cycles' than a classic genetic algorithm. Exact iteration counts per task not reported.
